headline: Highest risk is medium: ComfyUI can ingest files and write model/workflow assets, but Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a non-runnable docs repo with no direct execution path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces, while B can process workflows and files. The only plausible injection path is manual copy/paste or imported text from A into B, so the blast radius is limited and not default. No shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF an operator copies text from agent_a docs into agent_b prompts or workflow nodes, injection becomes possible.
IF agent_b is configured to parse imported text as instructions, attacker-controlled content from agent_a can influence execution.
mitigations: Keep agent_a content out of agent_b prompt fields.
Review imported workflow text before loading into agent_b.
Use a separate staging folder for any copied snippets.
Disable automatic prompt parsing in agent_b where available.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces. Agent_b is offline by default and only has vendor-only egress, with no secrets handled. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive-data flow between them, so leakage risk is limited to unusual operator-mediated copying.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files into agent_b's model/workflow directories, those files may be exposed to agent_b.
IF copied content from agent_a includes secrets or regulated data, it can be surfaced in agent_b outputs.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in shared folders.
Use separate OS accounts for the two agents.
Scan copied text for secrets before pasting.
Keep agent_b offline except when needed.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or network capabilities, so it cannot conflict on mutable resources by itself. B can write model-related files but cannot modify git state or spawn subprocesses, and no shared writable directory is documented. Any conflict would require unusual external orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory by an external orchestrator, file collisions can occur.
IF agent_b is given write access to assets that agent_a also edits manually, last-writer-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same workflow files.
Serialize writes through one operator account.
Back up shared assets before edits.
requires-engineering: add file locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated prompt-engineering resource, not an executing agent, so it does not autonomously generate actions. B can consume workflows and outputs, but there is no documented default path where B treats A's content as authoritative. The cascade is therefore manual and limited unless an operator imports A-derived text uncritically.
conditions: IF operator-supplied text from agent_a is inserted into agent_b workflows without review, B may act on incorrect instructions.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-run imported workflows, errors from copied content can cascade.
mitigations: Verify copied instructions before execution.
Use a human review step for imported workflows.
Test new workflows on dummy inputs first.
Keep agent_a as reference material only.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before workflow execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: A has no touched data classes or handling obligations, and B is offline by default with no secrets handled and no stated residency or retention mismatch. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented and no regulated data class is identified, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually introduced into agent_b, separate compliance review is required.
IF a deployment adds logging or retention beyond the documented profiles, reassess compliance.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review deployment logging settings.
Document data-handling boundaries.
Use separate retention policies if data is introduced.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
